Budded
BUD-ed
verb (past tense)
From bud, a shoot or unopened blossom, of uncertain Northern origin; hence to put forth buds. In Scripture the word carries the note of life appearing where none was expected — and, once, where none was possible.

Biblical Definition

To bud is to put forth the first shoot, the promise of fruit before the fruit. Scripture uses it of vines and pomegranates in their season (Gen 40:10; Son 6:11), but its great occurrence is a dead stick in a tabernacle. Korah, Dathan, and Abiram had risen against Moses and Aaron with the charge that all the congregation were holy, and wherefore then lift ye up yourselves above the congregation of the LORD? God answered first in judgment, and then, lest the question be reopened, He answered in a sign. Twelve rods, one for each tribe, Aaron’s among them, were laid up before the testimony, with the word: “the man’s rod, whom I shall choose, shall blossom” (Num 17:5). “And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds” (Num 17:8). Observe the piling of the stages: budded, buds, blossoms, almonds — a whole season in one night, on a cut branch that had no root and no soil. Eleven rods stayed dead. The priesthood is not seized, voted, or claimed by the sincerity of the claimant; it is given, and God vindicates His own appointment by making life come out of dead wood. That rod was kept in the ark for a token against the rebels (Heb 9:4).

Webster 1828 Definition

Put forth buds; used above all of Aaron’s rod, which budded, blossomed, and yielded almonds in a night to vindicate God’s appointed priesthood.

expand to see more

BUDDED, past tense of bud: to put forth or produce buds, shoots, or germs.

A bud is the gem or unopened shoot of a plant, containing the rudiments of leaf, flower, or branch.

Hebrew parach, to sprout or break forth into bloom (Num 17:8).

Used of the vine in Pharaoh’s butler’s dream (Gen 40:10) and of pomegranates in Son 6:11.

Num 17:8 records the budding of Aaron’s rod, laid up afterward in the ark (Heb 9:4).

Key Scripture

Num 17:8 — "And it came to pass, that on the morrow Moses went into the tabernacle of witness; and, behold, the rod of Aaron for the house of Levi was budded, and brought forth buds, and bloomed blossoms, and yielded almonds."

Heb 9:4 — "Which had the golden censer, and the ark of the covenant overlaid round about with gold, wherein was the golden pot that had manna, and Aaron's rod that budded, and the tables of the covenant;"

Gen 40:10 — "And in the vine were three branches: and it was as though it budded, and her blossoms shot forth; and the clusters thereof brought forth ripe grapes:"

Son 6:11 — "I went down into the garden of nuts to see the fruits of the valley, and to see whether the vine flourished, and the pomegranates budded."

Modern Corruption

Korah’s argument is perennial: since all the people are holy, no man may be set over them in the things of God. The budding rod is God’s standing answer, and it is the answer most resented.

expand to see more

Korah’s complaint sounds pious and is quotable to this day: all the congregation are holy, every one of them, and the LORD is among them — wherefore then lift ye up yourselves? Every generation reproduces it. If the priesthood of all believers is true, why any ordained office at all? If the Spirit indwells every Christian, why should any man be set apart to preach, and why should the qualifications for that office be laid down as narrowly as they are in 1Ti 3 and Tit 1? The budding rod is God’s reply, and He gave it in a form no argument can touch. He did not debate Korah; He put twelve dead sticks in the dark and let one of them bloom. The priesthood is His to bestow. Under the new covenant every believer indeed has access through the one great High Priest, and the Levitical order is fulfilled and abolished in Him; yet the same God who ended the shadow appointed elders in every church, and He no more permits a man to seize that office than He permitted Korah to seize Aaron’s. “No man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron” (Heb 5:4).

This entry faces no significant postmodern redefinition. The principle to recover is that God vindicates His own appointments by giving life where there is none. The rod was cut wood. It had no root, no earth, no water, and one night; and in the morning it was carrying almonds, while eleven identical sticks lay beside it exactly as dead as they had been laid down. That is the pattern of everything God does through His ministers. The word preached is a dead stick until He makes it bud; the man who preaches it is dust and ash; and where fruit appears, no one can mistake whose hand did it. Aaron’s rod was then laid up in the ark beside the pot of manna and the tables of the covenant — bread from heaven, law from heaven, and life from dead wood, all three sealed under the mercy seat. It is not a stretch to see the whole gospel in that box, nor to see, in a rod that lived after it was cut off, the Branch out of a dry ground who rose on the third day.

Greek & Hebrew Roots

To put forth the first shoot; supremely, a cut rod that budded, blossomed, and bore almonds in a night to seal God’s own choice.

expand to see more

Budded — past of bud, a shoot or unopened blossom; Hebrew parach, to break forth into bloom.

Num 17:5 — “the man’s rod, whom I shall choose, shall blossom”: the test God Himself set.

Num 17:8 — four stages in one night: budded, buds, blossoms, almonds; eleven rods stayed dead.

The almond is the first tree of the Hebrew spring — the waking tree, the tree of hastening.

Heb 9:4 — the rod is laid up in the ark with the manna and the tables of the covenant.

Usage

"God did not argue with Korah; He put twelve dead sticks in the dark and made one bloom."

"“No man taketh this honour unto himself, but he that is called of God, as was Aaron” (Heb 5:4)."

"Life out of cut wood is the pattern of all true ministry — no one can mistake whose hand did it."
